title: Conversations with an Executioner: a chilling classic reveals the mind of a Nazi mass murderer

paragraphs.en: In 1949, Kazimierz Moczarski, a leading member of the Polish resistance, was in his fourth year of incarceration when he was moved into a cell with two Nazis at Warsaw’s Mokotów prison. One of them was Jürgen Stroop – a war criminal and SS general who had led the infamous destruction of the Warsaw ghetto and was responsible for the murder or capture of more than 56,000 Jews. They shared the same four walls for 255 consecutive days.
paragraphs.zh: 1949 年，波兰抵抗运动的重要成员卡齐米日·莫恰尔斯基在入狱的第四年被转移到华沙莫科托夫监狱，与两名纳粹分子关在同一间牢房。其中一人是于尔根·施特鲁普——一名战犯和党卫军将军，曾指挥对华沙犹太人区的臭名昭著的摧毁行动，并对超过 5.6 万名犹太人的被杀或被俘负有责任。他们在这四面墙里共处了连续 255 天。

paragraphs.en: A celebrated figure in modern-day Poland, Moczarski was regarded as a threat to the power of the postwar communist regime in the country. Like other resistance members, he was accused of collaboration and arrested. But Moczarski, who spoke German, used his imprisonment with Stroop as an opportunity to investigate a question: what turned some Germans into mass murderers, seeking to impose their “ Ordnung ”, order, across the world? His book about the experience, Conversations with an Executioner, was published in 1977. An instant bestseller, it was performed as a play the same year, directed by Andrzej Wajda. It is finally being published in the UK this month, in its first uncensored translation into English by Sean Gasper Bye.
paragraphs.zh: 莫恰尔斯基在现代波兰是位知名人物，却被视为对该国战后共产主义政权权力的威胁。和其他抵抗运动成员一样，他被指控与敌合作并遭到逮捕。但会说德语的莫恰尔斯基把与施特鲁普同囚一室的机会用来探究一个问题：是什么让一些德国人变成了大规模屠杀者，试图把自己的“秩序”（Ordnung）强加给整个世界？他将这段经历写成了《与刽子手对话》一书，于 1977 年出版。该书一经出版即成畅销书，同年被改编成舞台剧，由安杰伊·瓦伊达执导。本月，它终于在英国出版，这是肖恩·加斯珀·拜翻译的第一个未删节英文版。

paragraphs.en: Publisher Clare Bullock heard about the book by chance nearly 10 years ago when she was studying Polish. “In one of my lessons, we were talking about books, Polish classics. And this wonderful teacher, he said, ‘Well, there’s this one book. I don’t understand why it’s never been published here. It’s absolutely extraordinary.’” It was not until she joined Duckworth Books as editorial director in 2024 that she had the opportunity to publish it. Next year is the 50th anniversary of the book’s publication and the 120th of Moczarski’s birth. There will be events to mark the occasion in Poland.
paragraphs.zh: 出版人克莱尔·布洛克大约 10 年前在学习波兰语时偶然听说了这本书。“在某一堂课上，我们聊到书籍、波兰经典。那位出色的老师说，‘嗯，有这么一本书，我不明白为什么它从未在这里出版。它绝对非同凡响。’”直到 2024 年她加入 Duckworth Books 担任编辑总监，才有了出版这本书的机会。明年将是该书出版 50 周年和莫恰尔斯基诞辰 120 周年，波兰将举办活动纪念这一时刻。

paragraphs.en: Stroop was an unrepentant fascist. He had been sentenced to death by the US military tribunal at Dachau and was awaiting trial in Poland. His cellmate Moczarski had been a member of the Home Army, the main resistance group, and had even taken part in plans to assassinate him. Yet Stroop told him his life story with little inhibition, from his rapid rise in the SS to the shocking details of the obliteration of the Warsaw ghetto in 1943.
paragraphs.zh: 施特鲁普是个拒不悔改的法西斯分子。他被达豪的美国军事法庭判处死刑，正在波兰等候审判。他的狱友莫恰尔斯基曾是主要抵抗组织“家乡军”的成员，甚至参与过刺杀他的计划。然而施特鲁普却毫无顾忌地向他讲述了自己的人生故事，从他在党卫军中的迅速崛起，到 1943 年摧毁华沙犹太人区的惊人细节。

paragraphs.en: The memoir offers a remarkable insight into the genesis and mindset of a Nazi war criminal. “Remember that Stroop lived in the shadow of the gallows,” Moczarski later said in an interview, “and this situation encourages people to talk.” The third man in the cell, Gustav Schielke, had been a low-ranking SS officer, who was not fully signed up to the Nazi cause, and he joined Moczarski in cross-questioning Stroop about his activities during the war. The highly charged relationship between the three men reads like a drama: they sparred with each other, but they also shared a solidarity as prisoners, becoming anxious when one of them was taken out of the cell for interrogation.
paragraphs.zh: 这本回忆录让人得以深入了解一名纳粹战犯的成因与心态。“记住，施特鲁普当时活在绞刑架的阴影之下，”莫恰尔斯基后来在接受采访时说，“这种处境会让人开口说话。”牢房里的第三个人古斯塔夫·席尔克曾是一名低级党卫军军官，并未完全认同纳粹事业，他与莫恰尔斯基一起盘问施特鲁普战时的所作所为。三人之间剑拔弩张的关系读起来像一出戏剧：他们相互交锋，但作为囚犯又有着同舟共济的情谊，其中一人被带出牢房审问时，另外两人都会感到不安。

paragraphs.en: Jürgen Stroop was executed in Poland in 1952, while Moczarski was released from prison in 1956. He wrote the book while working as a journalist and assiduously factchecked Stroop’s version of events. “My father tried to talk to publishers in the late 60s, but the book was banned, totally banned,” says Elżbieta Moczarska, who was born in 1958, the only child of Moczarski and his wife Zofia. Her mother was also in the resistance and was arrested after the war as well. “Everyone obviously wanted to hear about the Nazis, but nobody wanted to have information on why a hero, somebody who was very high in the resistance, was put into the same cell [as Nazis] and was imprisoned for such a long time.” It was finally serialised in a literary magazine in the early 70s and then published as a book after Moczarski’s death, with the permission of the Communist party, in a censored edition. Elżbieta spent nearly 40 years trying to get a complete translation published in English.
paragraphs.zh: 于尔根·施特鲁普于 1952 年在波兰被处决，而莫恰尔斯基于 1956 年获释出狱。他在从事记者工作期间写了这本书，并一丝不苟地核实了施特鲁普对事件的叙述。“我父亲在 60 年代末试图联系出版商，但这本书被禁了，完全被禁了，”1958 年出生的埃尔日别塔·莫恰尔斯卡说，她是莫恰尔斯基和妻子佐菲亚唯一的孩子。她的母亲也曾参加抵抗运动，战后同样被捕。“显然每个人都想听纳粹的故事，但没有人想了解为什么一位英雄、一个在抵抗运动中地位很高的人，会被关进（与纳粹）同一间牢房，并被囚禁那么长时间。”这本书最终在 70 年代初于一份文学杂志上连载，后来在莫恰尔斯基去世后，经共产党许可，以删节版的形式出版成书。埃尔日别塔花了近 40 年时间，试图让完整的英文译本得以出版。

paragraphs.en: Moczarski allowed Stroop to condemn himself in his own words. The Nazi unashamedly relived his genocidal glory days despite his hostile audience, holding forth about his life with such candour that he is sometimes as comic as he is chilling. In one memorable scene, Stroop demonstrated how to ride a horse in the prison cell, whinnying and snorting. His repeated lascivious references to women’s breasts are almost a running gag. “I think we all talk about Hannah Arendt and the banality of evil, but this is it in one man,” says Bullock.
paragraphs.zh: 莫恰尔斯基让施特鲁普用自己的话给自己定了罪。尽管面对的是充满敌意的听众，这名纳粹仍毫无愧色地重温他种族灭绝的辉煌岁月，如此坦率地高谈阔论自己的人生，以至于他有时既令人胆寒，又显得滑稽。在一个令人难忘的场景中，施特鲁普在牢房里演示如何骑马，又是嘶鸣又是喷鼻。他屡屡带着淫亵意味地提及女性的乳房，几乎成了一个反复出现的笑点。“我想我们都在谈论汉娜·阿伦特和‘平庸之恶’，但这就是体现在一个人身上的例子，”布洛克说。

paragraphs.en: It was not possible for Moczarski to take any notes in prison and he had to write the book from memory, so can his reports of the conversations with Stroop and Schielke be trusted as a reliable account? “My father built a kind of castle in his head,” says his daughter Elżbieta. “He could write in his head. He said once that for long-term prisoners the ability to hear is different and you learn to remember.” Moczarski said that he could replay his conversations with Stroop as if they were a tape recording. Bullock points to Solzhenitsyn’s similarly exceptional memory when imprisoned – he was able to compose and remember a poem of 7,000 lines in his head. “I think a lot of it must just have been astonishing recall backed up by serious research,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: 莫恰尔斯基在狱中无法做任何笔记，只能凭记忆写这本书，那么他对与施特鲁普和席尔克对话的记述能否被视为可靠的记录？“我父亲在脑海里搭建了一座城堡，”他的女儿埃尔日别塔说，“他能在脑子里写作。他曾说，对于长期囚犯来说，听的能力会有所不同，你会学会记忆。”莫恰尔斯基说，他能像回放录音带一样重现与施特鲁普的对话。布洛克提到了索尔仁尼琴在被囚禁时同样惊人的记忆力——他能在脑子里创作并记住一首 7000 行的诗。“我想，其中很大一部分一定只是惊人的记忆，并辅以认真的研究，”她说。
